name: Body wraps for weight loss

card.summary: Body wraps are mud, plastic, neoprene or sauna-suit wraps worn around the body, marketed for slimmer measurements and smoother-looking skin.
card.aka: mud wraps; plastic wraps; sauna suits; neoprene wraps
card.note: The FDA says any inch loss is temporary water loss; heavy sweating can cause dehydration.

quick.overview:
Body wraps cover the torso, waist or limbs with mud, bandages, plastic or neoprene, often under a sauna suit, to make the wearer sweat. They are marketed to slim and tone and to hydrate or firm the skin.

The visible result people report is a smaller tape measurement or tighter-feeling skin right after a session. The FDA states that any weight or inch loss comes from sweating and is temporary because fluid is replaced by drinking and eating.
quick.how: At spas, the wrap is applied for a set session, sometimes with mud, followed by bandages or a PVC suit to hold it in. At home, people wear neoprene or sauna-style wraps during exercise or rest. Results are usually judged by measuring right after the session.
quick.risks: Rapid heavy sweating can cause dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, according to the FDA. Heat, tight compression and long sessions add strain, so people with heart, kidney or heat-related conditions are generally advised by clinicians to ask first.

lead: Body wraps are treatments in which the body is covered, with mud, bandages, plastic or a sauna suit, to induce sweating and temporary tightening. Mud wraps are a spa treatment in which mud covers the skin for a period; bandages go over it, sometimes with a PVC sauna suit [1].

For looks, proponents say wraps slim and tone the body, hydrate or firm skin, relax muscles and help flush toxins through sweat [1]. People often use them before events because measurements can look smaller immediately afterward.

The FDA says weight or inch loss from wraps comes from sweating and is temporary, since fluid is quickly replaced, and that wraps have no effect on fat deposits [1]. Heavy fluid loss can lead to dehydration and electrolyte disturbance [1].

chain: Temporarily smaller measurements and firmer-feeling skin
angle.text: Wraps change measurements for a short time through fluid loss and compression. Spa versions also leave the skin feeling smooth and hydrated.

infobox: Mud wraps, plastic wraps, sauna suits, neoprene wraps

paras: Wraps are sold with claims of slimming, toning, hydrating and firming skin, easing sore joints and inflammation and removing toxins by sweat [1].
The FDA says any weight or inch loss from wraps comes from sweating and is temporary because the fluid is replaced; it states wraps have no effect on fat deposits [1].
Rapid, heavy fluid loss can cause severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance [1].
